chunks: Those who disbelieve spend their possessions on turning men away from God. They will go on spending and rue it in the end, and will be subdued. But those who remain disbelievers shall be gathered into Hell
ai.seo_question: What happens to the wealth of those who disbelieve and spend it to turn people away from God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the strategic use of wealth by the Quraysh to obstruct the propagation of Islam, framing their expenditure not as charity but as a tool of spiritual diversion. The promise of regret underscores the futility of material power against divine truth, a theme often linked to the concept of *Futuhat* (divine opening) where the weak are ultimately victorious over the wealthy. This narrative serves as a historical precedent for the resilience of the early Muslim community against economic and social pressures.
